question: Establishment Democrat?
headline: Mostly yes
summary: He votes with Chuck Schumer 95.9% of the time on votes where both voted Yea or Nay. Of his 38 splits, 26 are No votes on legislation Chuck Schumer backed, 9 are Yes votes on legislation Chuck Schumer opposed, 0 are Yes votes on nominees Chuck Schumer opposed and 3 are No votes on nominees Chuck Schumer backed. He votes with a majority of Senate Democrats 96.5% of the time, rank 12 of 47.
why: “Mostly yes” because he votes with the Democratic leader at least 90% of the time, the rule used here, and with a majority of Senate Democrats 96.5% of the time. His independence shows in the 38 votes where he split from Chuck Schumer. This card uses votes and campaign money only; it does not weigh appointments, party roles or endorsements.
tiles: Votes cast the same way as Chuck Schumer (920 votes where both voted Yea or Nay)
Party unity: votes with a majority of Senate Democrats (rank 12 of 47)
